leagues.name: DP World Tour (Race to Dubai)
notes: The 2026 Race to Dubai season runs 27 November 2025 (BMW Australian PGA Championship) to 15 November 2026 (DP World Tour Championship, Dubai); the official schedule page lists 42 tournaments plus a U.S. Open Final Qualifying row, which is not counted (europeantour.com/dpworld-tour/schedule, fetched 25 Sep 2026).

Season-labelled '2026-27' here because the season crosses calendar years (Nov 2025 - Nov 2026), matching the site's other cross-year competitions; the tour's own pages brand the season '2026 Race to Dubai'.

The tour is named for its Title Partner DP World, whose extension to 2035 is 'the largest in the Tour's history'; DP World also titles the season-ending DP World Tour Championship and is Official Partner to a further 15 tournaments a season (tour press release, 11 Nov 2025).

The five Rolex Series events in 2026 are the Hero Dubai Desert Classic, Genesis Scottish Open, BMW PGA Championship, Abu Dhabi Championship and DP World Tour Championship (rolex/2026 page, '5 unmissable events').

Gulf events: Dubai Invitational, Hero Dubai Desert Classic, Bapco Energies Bahrain Championship, Qatar Masters, Abu Dhabi Championship and DP World Tour Championship (all UAE except Bahrain and Qatar). No Saudi events in 2026; Ras Al Khaimah is not on the schedule.

Event titles change with sponsors (Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship is now the Abu Dhabi Championship; Commercial Bank Qatar Masters is now plain Qatar Masters); two events are 'presented by' sponsors (Magical Kenya Open presented by absa; Open de Espana presented by Madrid).

Shape note: tournaments are recorded as clubs (sportId golf, leagueId dp-world-tour). There are no shirt kits for tournaments; kits array is empty. Tournament title sponsors of events other than the four with their own deal rows are recorded in unsourced (event-host shape).

claims.text: DP World's ultimate owner is the Government of Dubai, whose federation, the UAE, sentenced 43 activists and dissidents to life imprisonment in a 2024 mass trial that rights groups called grossly unfair; the Federal Supreme Court upheld the convictions in March 2025.
claims.short: Government of Dubai owns DP World; UAE mass-trial life sentences upheld in 2025

source.name: DP World Annual Report 2025 (ownership) + Human Rights Watch (mass trial and upheld convictions)
source.note: Ownership from DP World Limited's FY2025 annual report (dp-world-ownership claim in normalized/claims.json); mass-trial facts from HRW.

claims.text: Bapco Energies is Bahrain's national integrated energy company, fronting the Kingdom's name on a DP World Tour event, while Human Rights Watch reports that in 2026 Bahraini authorities arbitrarily arrested dozens of people, that Mohammed Almosawi died in custody with signs of torture after being forcibly disappeared, and that 67 people had their citizenship stripped.
claims.short: Bahrain state energy company titles a tour event; HRW documents 2026 arrests, a death in custody, citizenship-stripping

source.name: Human Rights Watch - Bahrain country page

claims.text: The Qatar Masters is organised by the Qatar Golf Association, whose president credited the Qatar Olympic Committee's support; Amnesty International reports that Qatar's migrant workers remain exposed to exploitation despite kafala reform and that expression and assembly are tightly restricted.
claims.short: Qatar Masters run by the state golf federation; Amnesty documents migrant-worker exploitation and restricted expression

source.name: DP World Tour news (QGA launch announcement) + Amnesty International - Human rights in Qatar

proposedRatings.reasoning: The tour's title partner to 2035 and title partner of the season finale, ultimately owned by the Government of Dubai (per DP World's own FY2025 annual report). Dubai/UK state money on the tour's name: the UAE's 2024 mass-trial life sentences, upheld in 2025, put Dubai state branding at serious; severe is reserved for live armed conflict.

Already rated serious in the corpus (owned by Dubai's government via ICD); it is also in the DP World Tour partner bar, so the existing rating carries over to this target. Same UAE record: 43 life sentences in the 2024 mass trial, upheld in 2025.

Bahrain's national energy company titles the Bahrain Championship. State money: HRW's 2026 Bahrain reporting (arbitrary arrests, a torture-signed death in custody, citizenship-stripping, jailed rights defenders) puts a Kingdom's national company at serious under the rubric.

The organiser of the Qatar Masters sits inside Qatar's state sports system (its president thanks the Qatar Olympic Committee). If it is confirmed as a state body, Qatar's documented record (migrant-worker exploitation, restricted expression) rates serious; flagged for a human to confirm the ownership link first.
